# Overview

# Percona Operator for MySQL Based on Percona XtraDB Cluster

The **[Percona Operator for MySQL](https://github.com/percona/percona-xtradb-cluster-operator)** is a Kubernetes-native solution designed to simplify the deployment, management, and scaling of MySQL clusters built on Percona XtraDB Cluster (PXC). The Operator leverages Kubernetes’ orchestration capabilities to automate critical database management tasks, including cluster provisioning, backups, failover, and scaling.

**[Percona XtraDB Cluster (PXC)](https://www.percona.com/software/mysql-database/percona-xtradb-cluster)** is an open-source, enterprise-grade MySQL solution designed for high availability and data consistency. It uses virtually synchronous replication, so every node holds the same data. PXC provides fault tolerance, automated failover, and scalability, making it ideal for running highly available MySQL databases in mission-critical environments.

This provides the foundation for the Percona Operator for MySQL, enabling simplified deployment and management of Percona XtraDB Cluster within Kubernetes environments.

[Get started](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/quickstart.html) [What’s new in version 1.20.0](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/ReleaseNotes/Kubernetes-Operator-for-PXC-RN1.20.0.html)

______________________________________________________________________

## Key Features and Benefits

#### 1. **Automated Deployment and Scaling**

- Simplifies the creation of MySQL clusters with minimal configuration.
- Dynamically scales instances based on workload demands, optimizing resource usage.

#### 2. **High Availability**

- Keeps the cluster serving when a node fails: with three nodes, the cluster continues after one node is lost, and the proxy reroutes traffic. Clients may need to reconnect.
- Uses virtually synchronous replication to keep all nodes consistent.

#### 3. **Self-Healing**

- Detects and recovers from node failures automatically to maintain cluster health.
- Ensures operational continuity with minimal manual intervention.

#### 4. **Backup and Restore**

- Provides consistent, automated backups to cloud storage or local volumes.
- Enables quick recovery, ensuring data safety and business continuity.

#### 5. **Enhanced Security**

- Supports encryption for data at rest and in transit.
- Integrates with Kubernetes Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) for secure database operations.

#### 6. **Operational Simplification**

- Offers seamless integration with Kubernetes-native tools like [`kubectl`](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubectl/) .
- Streamlines database monitoring, management, and troubleshooting.

#### 7. **Flexibility for Cloud-Native Architectures**

- Optimized for public, private, and hybrid cloud deployments.
- Allows unified management of databases across diverse environments.

## Use Case

The **Percona Operator for MySQL** is ideal for various scenarios such as providing Database as a Service (DBaaS), ensuring high availability for mission-critical applications, scaling cloud-native applications, and implementing disaster recovery strategies. It is particularly useful for organizations with hybrid or multi-cloud infrastructures, where it simplifies the deployment and management of MySQL clusters across multiple environments. The Operator also benefits development and testing teams by enabling quick spin-up of MySQL clusters for testing and development purposes, helping to accelerate product development cycles and reduce operational overhead.

# About

# Design and architecture

This section explains how Percona Operator for MySQL based on Percona XtraDB Cluster is built: what runs in your Kubernetes cluster, which component is responsible for what, and how the pieces interact. Read it to build a mental model of the system, and come back to it when something fails and you need to know where to look first. If something is failing now, start with [Initial troubleshooting](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug.html). The [Glossary](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html) explains the Kubernetes and Galera terms used in this section.

## Percona XtraDB Cluster in brief

*Percona XtraDB Cluster* combines *Percona Server for MySQL* with the XtraDB storage engine, *Percona XtraBackup*, and the *[Galera](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#galera) library*. Galera provides virtually synchronous multi-primary replication: every node holds the full data set. A transaction commits after its write set is delivered to all nodes and passes certification. The other nodes apply it a moment later, so a read on another node can briefly return older data, unless you set the `wsrep_sync_wait` variable.

Use 3 to 5 nodes in production:

- **Not more than 5.** Every write must be confirmed by all nodes. More nodes mean more network round trips and acknowledgments for each transaction, which increases latency and resource usage.
- **An odd number.** Galera decides which nodes may keep serving queries by [quorum](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#quorum) voting. With an even number of nodes, a network partition can split the cluster into two equal halves. Neither half has a majority, so both stop serving queries to avoid data inconsistency.

With 3 nodes, the cluster keeps working when any one node goes down.

## How clients connect

Applications don’t connect to the database Pods directly. A proxy sits in front of the nodes and routes client connections.

Clients connect to a Kubernetes Service that sends traffic to a proxy, and the proxy routes it to the database nodes. You choose one of two proxies:

- **HAProxy** (default) is a TCP load balancer. It sends writes to one node and can spread reads across all nodes. Applications use the `cluster1-haproxy` Service for read-write traffic and `cluster1-haproxy-replicas` for reads.
- **ProxySQL** is SQL-aware. It understands MySQL traffic and can route queries by rules. Applications use the `cluster1-proxysql` Service for both reads and writes. See [What load balancer to use?](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/load-balancing.html#what-load-balancer-to-use).

The Operator creates more Services for its own use, such as the [headless Services](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#headless-service) that the cluster components use to find each other. See [Services and ports](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/services.html) for every Service, its ports and when it exists.

## The four layers

A running cluster is the combined result of four layers. Most confusion during troubleshooting comes from expecting one layer to do something that belongs to another. The [Who owns what](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-responsibilities.html) page covers each layer in detail.

```
flowchart TB
  U["<b>User</b><br/>Custom Resource, Secrets,<br/>CRDs and RBAC, node and storage capacity"]
  O["<b>Operator</b><br/>reconcile loop: compares the Custom Resource<br/>with the cluster and corrects differences"]
  K["<b>Kubernetes</b><br/>StatefulSets, scheduling, storage (CSI),<br/>networking and DNS, Pod lifecycle"]
  G["<b>Percona XtraDB Cluster / Galera</b><br/>replication, quorum, SST and IST"]
  U -- "writes the desired state" --> O
  O -- "creates and updates objects" --> K
  K -- "runs Pods and volumes for" --> G
  O -. "configures; recovers after a full crash" .-> G
```

- **User.** You describe the cluster you want in the `PerconaXtraDBCluster` [Custom Resource (CR)](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#custom-resource) and provide everything the Operator cannot create for you: the CustomResourceDefinitions (CRDs) and RBAC, credentials for backup storage, and enough nodes and storage to run the cluster.
- **Operator.** The Operator runs a reconcile loop. It reads the CR, compares it with what exists in Kubernetes, and creates, updates or deletes objects to close the gap. It repeats this about every five seconds. It also runs day-2 tasks such as ordered restarts, password changes, backups and recovery after a full cluster crash. See [How the Operator reacts to changes](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-reconciliation.html).
- **Kubernetes.** Kubernetes turns the objects the Operator creates into running Pods. It schedules Pods to nodes, provisions and attaches volumes through the CSI driver, provides Services and DNS, and restarts failed containers.
- **Percona XtraDB Cluster / Galera.** Inside the Pods, Galera replicates data between nodes, maintains quorum, and brings a joining node up to date with an [Incremental State Transfer (IST)](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#ist) or a full [State Snapshot Transfer (SST)](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#sst). The Operator writes the Galera configuration but does not control these mechanisms at runtime.

## Cluster topology

The following diagram shows a cluster named `cluster1` with three Percona XtraDB Cluster nodes, HAProxy, and point-in-time recovery turned on.

```
flowchart LR
  C[Clients] --> S1["Service<br/>cluster1-haproxy"]
  C --> S2["Service<br/>cluster1-haproxy-replicas"]
  S1 --> H["HAProxy Pods<br/>haproxy + pxc-monit"]
  S2 --> H
  H -- "writer, reads" --> P0["cluster1-pxc-0"]
  H -. "failover, reads" .-> P1["cluster1-pxc-1"]
  H -. "failover, reads" .-> P2["cluster1-pxc-2"]
  P0 <-- "Galera replication" --> P1
  P1 <-- "Galera replication" --> P2
  PITR["cluster1-pitr<br/>binlog collector"] -- "reads binlogs" --> P1
  PITR --> ST[("Backup storage<br/>S3 / Azure")]
  J["Backup Job xb-*"] -- "SST" --> P2
  J --> ST
```

Each node Pod has its own [PersistentVolumeClaim](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#pvc) (PVC) for the data directory. Galera replication runs between all node pairs; the diagram shows only two links for readability.

Here is how a client request reaches the data:

1. A client connects to the `cluster1-haproxy` Service on port 3306 for read-write traffic, or to `cluster1-haproxy-replicas` on port 3306 for reads. The replicas Service forwards port 3306 to port 3307 in the HAProxy Pods. See [Services and ports](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/services.html).
1. The Service forwards the connection to one of the HAProxy Pods.
1. HAProxy sends writes to `cluster1-pxc-0`. If that node fails its health check, HAProxy sends writes to another node. Read connections from the replicas Service are spread across nodes.
1. HAProxy learns which nodes exist through the headless `cluster1-pxc` Service. The `pxc-monit` container in each HAProxy Pod watches that Service in DNS and regenerates the HAProxy configuration when the set of nodes changes.
1. The node executes the transaction and Galera replicates it to the other nodes before the commit returns.

Node discovery doesn’t use the Kubernetes API. A small `peer-list` tool resolves the DNS SRV records of a headless Service every second and runs a script when the list of Pods changes:

- In the proxy Pods, `pxc-monit` watches `cluster1-pxc`, which lists only ready database Pods, and updates the proxy configuration.
- In the database Pods, the `pxc` container watches `cluster1-pxc-unready`, which also lists Pods that are not ready yet, to find the other nodes when it starts and builds the Galera cluster address from them.

See [Node discovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-workflows.html#node-discovery) for the timings and where to look when it fails.

Two more components appear around the nodes:

- **The binlog collector** (`cluster1-pitr` Deployment) exists only when point-in-time recovery is turned on. It reads binary logs from one node and uploads them to backup storage. At the start of each upload cycle, it looks up the nodes through `cluster1-pxc`, keeps those that are `Synced` and in the [primary component](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#primary-component), and picks the one whose oldest binlog is the oldest. This node most likely still has every binlog the collector hasn’t uploaded yet. If the current node becomes unhealthy, or another node has older binlogs, the collector switches to it and logs the reason. See [Point-in-time recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-workflows.html#point-in-time-recovery).
- **Backup Jobs** (`xb-<backup-name>`) exist only while a backup runs. By default, the Job joins the cluster as a Galera [arbitrator](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#arbitrator) and receives a full copy of the data from a [donor](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#donor) node through SST, then uploads it to storage. With the `XtrabackupSidecar` [feature gate](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/env-vars-operator.html#pxco_feature_gates) turned on (a tech preview feature), each database Pod runs an extra `xtrabackup` container instead. The backup Job asks this sidecar on a non-primary node to run XtraBackup on the local data, so no node enters the `Donor` state. See [Backup methods](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-methods.html).

If you use ProxySQL instead of HAProxy, the picture is the same with `cluster1-proxysql` in place of `cluster1-haproxy`. There is no separate replicas Service, because ProxySQL splits reads and writes by its own rules. See [Services and ports](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/services.html).

With `proxysql.scheduler.enabled`, ProxySQL uses the external [`pxc_scheduler_handler`](https://docs.percona.com/proxysql/psh-overview.html) instead of its built-in Galera support. The scheduler checks the nodes, keeps exactly one writer, and spreads `SELECT` queries across all nodes, or across all nodes except the writer when `proxysql.scheduler.writerIsAlsoReader` is `false`. With the scheduler enabled, the ProxySQL instances no longer form a ProxySQL cluster, and the `proxysql-monit` container is not created. See [ProxySQL scheduler](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/proxysql-conf.html#proxysql-scheduler-tech-preview).

The [Key workflows](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-workflows.html) page describes proxy failover, backups, restores and crash recovery step by step.

### Scheduling and storage

To survive a node failure, the Operator places the database Pods on separate Kubernetes nodes with [Pod anti-affinity](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/#affinity-and-anti-affinity) . By default, this rule is *required*: with three database Pods you need at least three schedulable nodes, or a Pod stays `Pending`. See [Control Pod scheduling](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/constraints.html) to change it.

If a Kubernetes node fails, Kubernetes can recreate the Pod on another node, but for a [StatefulSet](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#statefulset) Pod it does so only after the failed Node object is removed or the stuck Pod is force-deleted. The Operator does neither. The Pod’s data lives in a PersistentVolume, so the storage must be able to follow the Pod: the Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver and StorageClass must support attaching the volume on a different node. A volume that can attach only in one zone keeps the Pod in that zone.

## What gets created

For a cluster named `cluster1`, the Operator creates StatefulSets for the database and the proxy, Services, Secrets, ConfigMaps, [PodDisruptionBudgets](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#pdb) and PersistentVolumeClaims. Jobs and the binlog collector exist only while a backup, a restore or point-in-time recovery needs them. PVCs and Secrets are not owned by the Custom Resource, so deleting the cluster doesn’t delete them.

- [Services and ports](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/services.html) lists every Service, its ports, and when it exists.
- [Objects the Operator creates](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/objects-created.html) lists all other objects, the [finalizers](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#finalizer) that clean them up, and the containers in each Pod.

# Who owns what

When something happens in the cluster, the question is which layer reacts: the Operator, Percona XtraDB Cluster ([Galera](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#galera)), Kubernetes, or you. This page answers it at a glance. For the detail of what you do and what the Operator does in each area, and for what never to change by hand, see [Responsibilities by area](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html). For an overview of the layers, see [Design and architecture](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture.html#the-four-layers).

Two rules explain most of the behavior:

- **You change the cluster only through the [Custom Resource](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#custom-resource) and the user Secrets.** The Operator turns them into Kubernetes objects, and reverts manual changes to the fields it manages.
- **Each layer keeps its own part alive.** Kubernetes keeps Pods running, Galera keeps the data consistent, and the Operator keeps the objects and the day-2 tasks matching the Custom Resource.

## Who reacts when something happens

| Event                                                          | Who reacts                                                                                                                                                        | Where it is explained                                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A container crashes or fails its liveness probe                | The kubelet restarts the container                                                                                                                                | [Health checks and probes](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-probes.html)                                   |
| A Pod is deleted or evicted                                    | The StatefulSet controller recreates it. The Operator isn’t involved                                                                                              | [In-cluster failover](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/failover-in-cluster.html)                                        |
| A Kubernetes node fails                                        | Kubernetes. A StatefulSet Pod is recreated elsewhere only after the Node object is removed or the stuck Pod is force-deleted, which is up to you or your platform | [Kubernetes](#kubernetes)                                                                                                                                  |
| A database node falls behind or rejoins                        | Galera, with IST or SST                                                                                                                                           | [Rejoining the cluster](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/failover-in-cluster.html#rejoining-the-cluster)                |
| A proxy loses a database node                                  | The proxy health check. The `pxc-monit` container updates the proxy configuration                                                                                 | [Key workflows](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-workflows.html#client-traffic-and-proxy-failover)         |
| The survivor of a 2-of-3 loss is outside the primary component | Liveness restarts it. When no node is in a primary component, the Operator starts the node with the highest `seqno` as a new one                                  | [Full cluster crash recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-workflows.html#full-cluster-crash-recovery) |
| You edit the Custom Resource                                   | The Operator reconciles the change                                                                                                                                | [How the Operator reacts to changes](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-reconciliation.html)                 |
| Someone edits an object the Operator manages                   | The Operator reverts the fields it manages                                                                                                                        | [Change the cluster through the Custom Resource](#change-the-cluster-through-the-custom-resource)                                                          |
| A scheduled backup is due                                      | The Operator creates the backup object, and a Job runs it                                                                                                         | [Scheduled backups](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-workflows.html#scheduled-backups)                     |
| A certificate expires and cert-manager isn’t used              | You                                                                                                                                                               | [Update certificates](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/tls-update.html)                                                 |
| A disk fills up                                                | You. With storage autoscaling on, the Operator grows the volume                                                                                                   | [Automatic storage resizing](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/scaling-storage-resize.html#automatic-storage-resizing)   |

## Change the cluster through the Custom Resource

A [Custom Resource](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/extend-kubernetes/api-extension/custom-resources/) (CR) is the Kubernetes object that describes the cluster you want. It is a blueprint that the Operator uses to deploy and manage your cluster.

**The Custom Resource is the source of truth. Change the cluster by editing the CR.**

The Operator compares the CR against what is running about every five seconds and corrects any difference it finds. A change you make directly to a [StatefulSet](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#statefulset), a Service, a Pod, or a managed Secret is drift. The Operator overwrites it, usually within seconds. If a change survives, this means the Operator does not manage that field yet. This doesn’t mean the change was accepted.

- **Edits to the fields the Operator manages do not persist.** The Operator reverts them and doesn’t raise an event.
- **Edits outside the CR can still cause damage before they are reverted.**

## Review responsibilities at a glance

The following table shows what the Operator handles and what stays with you. Select an area for the details and the list of manual actions to avoid.

| Area                                                                                                                                                                         | Operator                                                                                                                                                                                | You                                                                                                     | Don’t do manually                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Cluster lifecycle](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#cluster-lifecycle)                                          | - Creates and heals StatefulSets, Services, and PodDisruptionBudgets. - Rolls out changes with ordered restarts. Kubernetes restarts failed Pods. - Recovers from a full cluster crash. | - Choose the cluster size. - Decide when to pause. - Plan maintenance windows.                          | - Scale or edit the StatefulSet. - Delete Pods to restart a node. - Remove finalizers.             |
| [Backups](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#back-up-the-database)                                                 | - Runs scheduled and on-demand backups. - Enforces deadlines. - Suspends backups on an unhealthy cluster.                                                                               | - Verify that backups restore. - Set retention. - Keep off-cluster copies.                              | - Delete a running backup Job. - Run `xtrabackup` by hand against a node.                          |
| [Restore and point-in-time recovery (PITR)](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#restore-and-point-in-time-recovery) | - Pauses the cluster, restores, and restarts it. - Detects binary log gaps.                                                                                                             | - Take a new full backup after a gap. - Pick the restore target.                                        | - Edit the cluster CR during a restore. - Run two restores at once.                                |
| [TLS](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#manage-certificates)                                                      | - Issues certificates. - Renews them **only via cert-manager**. - Applies rotations without downtime.                                                                                   | - Rotate certificates yourself if cert-manager is not installed. - Manage any certificate you supplied. | - Edit the `ssl` or `ssl-internal` Secrets in place. - Delete them to re-issue certificates.       |
| [Users and secrets](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#users-and-secrets)                                          | - Creates the system users with the cluster. - Applies the passwords you change in the Secret to MySQL and the proxies.                                                                 | - Set passwords in the user Secret. - Manage your own application users.                                | - Run `ALTER USER` on a system user in MySQL. - Edit the `internal-` Secret. - Drop a system user. |
| [Storage](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#storage)                                                              | - Grows Persistent Volume Claims (PVCs) when the CR asks, and automatically when autoscaling is on.                                                                                     | - Pick a StorageClass that supports expansion. - Watch capacity.                                        | - Resize or delete PVCs by hand. - Shrink storage.                                                 |
| [Cross-site replication](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#cross-site-replication)                                | - Sets up the replication channels from the CR. - Removes channels that are not in the CR. - Logs when a channel isn’t running.                                                         | - Provide routable endpoints and matching replication passwords. - Monitor replication and repair it.   | - Create replication channels in MySQL by hand.                                                    |
| [Upgrades](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#database-upgrades)                                                   | - Coordinates version upgrades node by node and keeps quorum.                                                                                                                           | - Decide when to upgrade. - Run major version upgrades as a planned change.                             | - Bypass SmartUpdate. - Edit image tags to jump a major version.                                   |

## The Operator

The Operator reads the Custom Resource, compares it with what exists in Kubernetes about every five seconds, and creates, updates or deletes objects to close the gap. It also runs the day-2 tasks: ordered restarts ([Smart Update](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-reconciliation.html#update-strategies)), password changes, certificates, storage resizing, backups, restores, point-in-time recovery, cross-site replication channels, and [recovery after a full cluster crash](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-workflows.html#full-cluster-crash-recovery).

**The Operator does not:**

- Control Galera at runtime. It writes the Galera configuration, but [quorum](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#quorum), [SST](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#sst) and [IST](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#ist), and [donor](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#donor) selection are handled by Galera itself.
- Handle Kubernetes node failures. It does not force-delete Pods stuck on a failed node or react to node taints. Kubernetes recreates a Pod from an unreachable node elsewhere only after the Node object is removed or the stuck Pod is force-deleted.
- Validate MySQL options. The contents of `spec.pxc.configuration` go into a ConfigMap as is.
- Install or upgrade CRDs and RBAC.
- Drop database users that you remove from `spec.users`.
- Repair broken cross-site replication. It only logs that the replication channel is not running.
- Renew self-signed certificates it generated without cert-manager.
- Report most problems as Kubernetes events. It emits events only for full cluster crash recovery, CA certificate rotation, and volume resize. Everything else is in the Operator logs and the Custom Resource status.

For each area in detail, see [Responsibilities by area](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html). For the objects the Operator creates, see [Objects the Operator creates](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/objects-created.html) and [Services and ports](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/services.html).

## Percona XtraDB Cluster and Galera

**Galera does:**

- Replicate every transaction to all nodes and certify it, resolving write conflicts.
- Maintain quorum and decide which nodes form the [primary component](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#primary-component) that serves queries.
- Slow down writes with flow control when a node falls behind.
- Bring a joining node up to date: with IST from another node’s write-set cache ([gcache](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#gcache)) if possible, or with a full SST through Percona XtraBackup otherwise. Galera also chooses the donor node.

**What the Operator sets up for Galera:**

- The list of peers to connect to, from the cluster DNS.
- A preferred list of SST donors that excludes `cluster1-pxc-0` (the HAProxy writer) and the node with the highest number.
- `pc.weight=10`, unless you set it yourself.
- Encryption of replication traffic when internal TLS certificates exist.
- `innodb_buffer_pool_size` and `max_connections` calculated from the Pod resources, unless you set them yourself. This requires a memory limit (`pxc.resources.limits.memory`). See [Auto-tuning MySQL options](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/options.html#auto-tuning-mysql-options).

**Health as the Pod probes see it:**

- A database Pod is *ready* only when its node belongs to the primary component and is `Synced`. A node that is a donor counts as ready by default. Set the `AVAILABLE_WHEN_DONOR` environment variable of the `pxc` container to a value other than `1` to make a donor not ready. HAProxy’s own health check has a separate switch, `OK_IF_DONOR`, which is off by default. See [In-cluster failover](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/failover-in-cluster.html#traffic-rerouting).
- The liveness probe tolerates long startups, SST and recovery, so a node that is busy catching up is not killed. A node that stays outside the primary component for about 30 seconds is restarted.
- See [Health checks and probes](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-probes.html) for what the probes check and who acts on their result.

**What this means in practice:**

- A Pod that is `Running` but not `Ready` usually means Galera hasn’t finished bringing the node in: the node is still receiving an SST or IST, or it cannot reach the other nodes.
- An SST that keeps failing stops after `pxc.sstRetryCount` attempts, and the Pod stays not ready until you intervene. See [Limit SST retries](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/sst-retry-limit.html).
- A bad option in `spec.pxc.configuration` shows up as `mysqld` failing to start, in the `pxc` container logs.

## Kubernetes

**Kubernetes does:**

- **Schedule Pods.** The Operator only writes the affinity rules, node selectors, tolerations, priority class and topology spread constraints you specify. The default anti-affinity is *required* on `kubernetes.io/hostname`: three database Pods need three schedulable nodes. Otherwise a Pod stays `Pending`, and after about a minute the Custom Resource status shows the scheduler’s message.
- **Provide storage.** The CSI driver and StorageClass provision volumes, bind them to zones, and expand file systems. A ReadWriteOnce volume ties the Pod to the node or zone where the volume can attach.
- **Run the network and DNS.** The database nodes find each other, and the proxies find the database nodes, by looking up the [headless Services](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#headless-service) in cluster DNS. If DNS is broken, nodes cannot form or join the cluster, proxies lose their backends, and crash detection stops working.
- **Provision load balancers.** For `LoadBalancer` Services, the cloud provider creates the load balancer. Firewalls and source ranges are yours and the provider’s to manage.
- **Manage the Pod lifecycle.** Run probes, restart failed containers, enforce [PodDisruptionBudgets](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#pdb) during node drains, and retry failed Jobs.
- **Collect garbage.** Delete objects owned by the Custom Resource when you delete it.

**Kubernetes does not:**

- Know anything about Galera beyond the [probes](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-probes.html). A native StatefulSet rolling update waits for each Pod to become ready, but it doesn’t pause for a running backup, doesn’t wait for ProxySQL to bring the node back online, and doesn’t stop early when a Pod can’t start.
- Expand a volume whose StorageClass doesn’t allow it, or beyond your storage quota.

## You, the user

The Operator keeps the cluster matching the Custom Resource. Everything it cannot create or decide for you stays with you:

- Install and upgrade the CRDs and RBAC, which the Operator never applies. See [Upgrade CRD and the Operator](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/update-operator.html).
- Provide capacity: enough schedulable nodes for the anti-affinity rules, and a StorageClass that allows volume expansion. See [Cluster lifecycle](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#cluster-lifecycle) and [Storage](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#storage).
- Provide credentials: the passwords in the user Secret, the backup storage credentials, and the PMM token. See [Users and Secrets](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#users-and-secrets).
- Renew certificates when cert-manager isn’t installed, or when you supplied them. See [Manage certificates](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#manage-certificates).
- Verify that backups restore, set retention, and keep copies outside the cluster storage. See [Back up the database](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#back-up-the-database).
- Monitor cross-site replication, and repair it when it breaks. See [Cross-site replication](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#cross-site-replication).
- Decide when to pause, upgrade, and restore. See [Database upgrades](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#database-upgrades) and [Restore and point-in-time recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#restore-and-point-in-time-recovery).

## Unsafe configurations

The Operator refuses configurations that put availability or data at risk, such as fewer than three database nodes or running without TLS. See [Stay inside safe operating limits](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#stay-inside-safe-operating-limits). To use one anyway, you opt in with a flag in the `spec.unsafeFlags` subsection. See [Override a safety check](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator-boundaries.html#override-a-safety-check).

## How to tell which layer it is

Check these sources in order. Each one narrows down the layer.

1. **Custom Resource status and conditions.** `kubectl get pxc cluster1 -o yaml` shows the cluster state, the reconcile error message if any, and scheduling problems. An `error` state with a spec message points to the user. See [Status](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-reconciliation.html#status).
1. **Events.** `kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp` shows Kubernetes problems: scheduling, volume attachment and resize, image pulls, probe failures. The Operator itself adds events only for full cluster crash recovery, CA rotation and volume resize. See [Check the events](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug-events.html).
1. **Operator logs.** `kubectl logs deployment/percona-xtradb-cluster-operator` shows what the Operator is doing or waiting for: a stuck rolling restart, a skipped backup, broken replication. Most Operator problems appear only here.
1. **Pod and container logs.** `kubectl logs cluster1-pxc-0 -c pxc` shows Galera and MySQL problems: SST failures, quorum loss, `mysqld` start failures. For backup and restore problems, read the logs of the Job. See [Check the logs](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug-logs.html).
