# Operator responsibilities by area

For each area, this page lists what the Operator does, what you still do, and which manual actions can damage a running cluster. For the layers, the events that trigger each one, and a table of all areas, see [Who owns what](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-responsibilities.html).

The Custom Resource is the source of truth: change the cluster by editing it. See [Change the cluster through the Custom Resource](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-responsibilities.html#change-the-cluster-through-the-custom-resource).

## Cluster lifecycle

Change cluster size, pause state, and deletion through the CR. Direct edits to the StatefulSet fight the next reconcile.

**What the Operator does:**

- Creates and reconciles the Percona XtraDB Cluster StatefulSet, the HAProxy or ProxySQL StatefulSet, their Services, and a PodDisruptionBudget for each of them.
- Leaves restarting failed Pods and containers to Kubernetes, and resynchronizing nodes to Galera. The Operator itself steps in only for a full cluster crash and for the rolling restarts it starts.
- Shuts the cluster down in order when you set `spec.pause: true`, and brings it back when you set it to `false`. Data is retained. See [Pause/resume Percona XtraDB Cluster](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/pause.html).
- Deletes resources in a safe order on cluster deletion, using finalizers. See [Delete the database cluster](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/delete.html#delete-the-database-cluster).
- Handles **full cluster crash recovery.** When every node is down and waiting, the Operator finds the node with the highest transaction sequence number and bootstraps from it. This behavior is on by default (`spec.pxc.autoRecovery`). See [Crash recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/recovery.html).

**What you still do:**

- Choose the cluster size. Stay inside the limits in [Stay inside safe operating limits](#stay-inside-safe-operating-limits).
- Decide when to pause a cluster, and for how long.
- Plan capacity, node size, and maintenance windows for any change that restarts Pods. Provide enough schedulable nodes for the Pod anti-affinity rules (by default, three database Pods need three nodes), and resource requests and limits that fit them. See [Control Pod scheduling](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/constraints.html).
- Check and tune MySQL options before you put them in `spec.pxc.configuration`. The Operator doesn’t validate them. See [Changing MySQL options](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/options.html).
- Decide whether to set the deletion finalizers. Without `percona.com/delete-pxc-pvc` and `percona.com/delete-ssl`, PVCs, Secrets and certificates remain after you delete the cluster, and you delete them yourself. ProxySQL PVCs are kept, also when you disable ProxySQL, unless you set `percona.com/delete-proxysql-pvc`. See [Clean up resources](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/delete.html#clean-up-resources).
- **Manual recovery when the Operator refuses to recover automatically.** The Operator does not bootstrap from a node when the cluster UUID or sequence number has regressed since the last recovery, because that bootstrap can lose data. It emits an `AutomaticRecoveryRefused` event and stops. That handover is deliberate. A restore also triggers it, because a restore creates a new UUID. See [When the Operator refuses automatic recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/recovery.html#when-the-operator-refuses-automatic-recovery). Don’t force a bootstrap. If you are not sure why the UUID changed, follow [Manual crash recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/recovery.html#manual-crash-recovery).

**Never do this manually:**

| Do not                                                                          | What goes wrong                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Do this instead                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Run `kubectl scale` or `kubectl edit` on the Percona XtraDB Cluster StatefulSet | The next reconcile reverts the change. If the change takes effect first, nodes can leave the cluster in the wrong order                                                                                                                                            | Change `spec.pxc.size` in the CR                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Remove a finalizer to finish a stuck delete                                     | Finalizers on the cluster shut nodes down in order and clean up PVCs and certificates. The `percona.com/delete-backup` finalizer on a backup removes the backup files from storage. Removing a finalizer abandons that cleanup and can orphan data or backup files | Find out why the finalizer is blocked. The cluster has four finalizers: `percona.com/delete-pxc-pods-in-order`, `percona.com/delete-pxc-pvc`, `percona.com/delete-proxysql-pvc`, and `percona.com/delete-ssl`. A backup can carry `percona.com/delete-backup`. Don’t remove the `internal.percona.com` finalizers either: the Operator adds and removes them itself |
| Run `kubectl delete pxc` to reset a misbehaving cluster                         | Depending on the finalizers set, this deletes the PVCs and the data on them                                                                                                                                                                                        | Pause the cluster and investigate                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Bootstrap Galera by hand while the Operator is running                          | The Operator is also trying to recover. Two bootstraps mean two clusters and a split brain                                                                                                                                                                         | Let auto-recovery run. Recover manually only after the Operator has refused and reported that refusal, or when `pxc.autoRecovery` is `false`                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

## Back up the database

Create backups through a schedule on the cluster CR or through a `PerconaXtraDBClusterBackup` resource. See [About backups](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups.html).

**What the Operator does:**

- Runs scheduled backups from `spec.backup.schedule`, and on-demand backups from a `PerconaXtraDBClusterBackup` resource.
- Applies retention to scheduled backups. With `retention` set, it deletes the oldest `Succeeded` backups beyond the configured count.
- Enforces deadlines so a backup cannot hang forever: `startingDeadlineSeconds`, `runningDeadlineSeconds`, and `suspendedDeadlineSeconds`. A backup that exceeds one is marked failed.
- Collects binary logs continuously for point-in-time recovery when `spec.backup.pitr` is enabled. See [Store binary logs for point-in-time recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-pitr.html).
- **Refuses to back up an unhealthy cluster.** If the cluster is not Ready, the backup does not start. A backup that is already running is suspended until the cluster recovers.

**What you still do:**

- **Verify that your backups restore.** The Operator confirms that a backup completed. It does not confirm that the backup is usable. Restore-test on a schedule. See [Restore the cluster from a previously saved backup](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-restore.html).
- Set retention, and keep any copies outside the cluster storage target.
- Manage credentials and lifecycle policies on the S3 or Azure bucket. Provide the storage credentials (S3 or Azure Secrets, or an IAM role), and a CA bundle for custom S3 endpoints.
- Keep binary logs on the servers long enough for the collector to upload them, if you use point-in-time recovery. See [Store binary logs for point-in-time recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-pitr.html).
- Decide whether a backup during a degraded window is worth the risk.

**Never do this manually:**

| Do not                                                                    | What goes wrong                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Do this instead                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Delete the backup Job to clear a stuck backup                             | The backup resource still reports that it is running, and storage may hold a partial backup that looks complete                                                                                                                                    | Let the deadline fail it, or delete the `PerconaXtraDBClusterBackup` resource. See [Delete the unneeded backup](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-delete.html) |
| Raise or remove the deadlines so backups stop failing                     | Deadlines are what stop a wedged backup from blocking upgrades indefinitely. SmartUpdate does not start while a backup is running                                                                                                                  | Find out why the backup is slow or stuck                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Set `unsafeFlags.backupIfUnhealthy` to get a backup from a broken cluster | A backup from a cluster that is not in sync may be inconsistent and may not restore                                                                                                                                                                | Repair the cluster, then back up. If you must take the backup, treat the result as best-effort only                                                                                                      |
| Run `xtrabackup` by hand against a Pod                                    | The manual backup runs outside the Operator’s control. It can overlap with an Operator backup, because the backup lock exists only with `backup.allowParallel: false` and a manual run doesn’t take it, and it loads a node the cluster depends on | Create a `PerconaXtraDBClusterBackup` resource                                                                                                                                                           |
| Delete objects from the backup storage bucket by hand                     | The PITR chain between a full backup and its binary logs breaks                                                                                                                                                                                    | Delete the `PerconaXtraDBClusterBackup` resource and let the finalizer clean up                                                                                                                          |

## Restore and point-in-time recovery

**What the Operator does:**

- Runs the whole restore sequence: pauses the cluster, runs the restore, starts the cluster, verifies that it is Ready, and marks the restore succeeded.
- Restores to a point in time by GTID, transaction, or timestamp.
- **Refuses concurrent restores.** A second restore against the same cluster fails immediately, so it does not corrupt the first.
- **Detects binary log gaps.** If the binlog collector finds that binary logs it needs are missing, it marks the most recent successful backup with the condition `PITRReady: False` and the reason `BinlogGapDetected`.

**What you still do:**

- Choose the restore target, and accept the data loss between that target and now.
- Plan the maintenance window. A restore stops the cluster.
- **Remove the recovery record after a restore.** A restore starts a new Galera cluster with a new UUID, and the Operator doesn’t reset `status.recovery`. If the Operator recovered the cluster automatically before, the next full cluster crash is refused until you remove the record. See [Remove the recovery record after the restore](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-restore-in-place.html#remove-the-recovery-record-after-the-restore).
- **Take a new full backup after a binlog gap is reported.** The gap means PITR from that backup is no longer possible, and the window it covers is unrecoverable. Nothing restores that window. Take a fresh full backup to start a new PITR chain.

**Never do this manually:**

| Do not                                               | What goes wrong                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Do this instead                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Edit the cluster CR while a restore is running       | **The restore controller writes to your CR.** It sets `spec.pause` to `true` to stop the cluster. During a point-in-time restore, it also sets `spec.pxc.size` to 1, the proxy sizes to 0, and `unsafeFlags.pxcSize` and `unsafeFlags.proxySize` to `true`. It writes your original values back from the restore resource status afterwards. An edit in that window is overwritten, or it is merged into a cluster that does not match the restore recorded state | Wait until the restore reaches `Succeeded` or `Failed`         |
| Unpause the cluster during a restore                 | The restore is operating on the data directory of stopped nodes. Starting them mid-restore can leave inconsistent data                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Wait                                                           |
| Start a second restore because the first looks stuck | The Operator rejects the second restore and marks it failed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Wait for the previous restore                                  |
| Delete the restore resource mid-flight               | The cluster stays paused. In a point-in-time restore, it can also stay at one database node with no proxies and the unsafe flags set. The Operator keeps your original values in the restore resource status, so deleting the resource deletes them too                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Let the restore finish, then delete the resource               |
| Ignore `PITRReady: False`                            | You believe you have point-in-time coverage that does not exist. You find out during an incident                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Take a new full backup, then confirm that the condition clears |

## Manage certificates

How certificates are renewed depends on who created them. See [Transport Layer Security (TLS)](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/TLS.html).

**What the Operator does:**

- Issues certificates when the cluster is created: through cert-manager when it is available, and self-signed when it is not.

- **Renews certificates automatically — but only when cert-manager manages them.**

- Re-issues leaf certificates when the CA changes, for cert-manager-managed certificates.

- Applies a certificate rotation to a running cluster without downtime. You place the new material in a Secret named `<secret-name>-new`. The Operator moves through the rotation in steps:

  - combines the old and new certificate authority (CA),
  - swaps the leaf certificate and key,
  - drops the old CA.

  See [Update certificates](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/tls-update.html#update-valid-certificates-without-downtime).

**What you still do:**

**If cert-manager is not installed, Operator-generated certificates are not renewed automatically.** Starting with version 1.19.0, these certificates are valid for 90 days, and the CA for three years. Check their actual [expiration dates](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/tls-update.html#check-your-certificates-for-expiration) and provide replacements before they expire. Expired certificates can prevent nodes from trusting each other and stop replication.

**If you supplied the TLS Secret yourself, renewal is your responsibility.** The Operator does not renew those certificates automatically, but it can apply replacements you provide through the `<secret-name>-new` rotation procedure. See [Generate certificates manually](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/tls-manual.html) and [Update certificates](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/tls-update.html#update-valid-certificates-without-downtime).

Watch expiry dates in both of these cases, and rotate before they are reached.

**Recommendation:** install [cert-manager](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/tls-cert-manager.html) for automatic certificate renewal. Otherwise, schedule a reminder based on your certificates’ actual expiration dates and rotate well before expiry with the `-new` Secret procedure in [Update certificates](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/tls-update.html).

**Never do this manually:**

| Do not                                                                     | What goes wrong                                                                                                                                                              | Do this instead                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Edit `tls.crt` or `tls.key` in the `ssl` or `ssl-internal` Secret directly | Nodes pick up a new certificate at different times. The nodes that have not restarted cannot talk to the nodes that have                                                     | Create the `<secret-name>-new` Secret and let the Operator roll it out    |
| Delete the TLS Secrets to force a re-issue                                 | The cluster loses the ability to communicate between nodes until new certificates exist and every node has restarted. On a running cluster, this is an outage                | Use the `-new` Secret rotation procedure                                  |
| Set `unsafeFlags.tls: true` to work around an expired certificate          | This only permits TLS to be disabled; it does not renew certificates or change `spec.tls.enabled`. Disabling TLS removes encryption and causes downtime on a running cluster | Rotate the certificate                                                    |
| Change the CA without rotating the leaf certificates                       | Nodes reject each other’s certificates                                                                                                                                       | Rotate both. The Operator does this for you when cert-manager issued them |

## Users and Secrets

**What the Operator does:**

- Creates the system users `root`, `operator`, `monitor`, `xtrabackup`, and `replication` when it creates the cluster. It also manages `proxyadmin` and the PMM users. See [System users](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/users.html#system-users).
- Propagates a password change. You edit the Secret named in `spec.secretsName`, and the Operator applies it in MySQL, updates the proxies, and restarts what needs restarting. It tracks what it has already applied in a separate Secret named `internal-<cluster-name>`.
- Manages application users declared in `spec.users`, including their grants and the databases they can reach.
- Rejects a user in `spec.users` whose name collides with a system user.

**What you still do:**

- Generate and store strong passwords, and decide when to rotate them.
- **Schedule password rotations.** Changing a system user’s password causes a rolling restart of the affected components. Treat it as a maintenance operation, not a routine edit.
- Change system-user passwords in the Secret named by `spec.secretsName`. See [Users](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/users.html).
- Declare application users in `spec.users`. The Operator creates them only when the cluster is `ready`. Removing an entry doesn’t drop the user from the database, so drop it yourself. See [Users](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/users.html).
- Provide the PMM token, if you use Percona Monitoring and Management. See [Monitor with PMM](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/monitoring.html).
- Manage application users you create directly in MySQL, outside `spec.users`. The Operator does not know about them and does not recreate them after a restore.

**Never do this manually:**

| Do not                                                                                  | What goes wrong                                                                                                                                          | Do this instead                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| Run `ALTER USER` on a system user inside MySQL                                          | The Operator still holds the old password, loses access to the cluster, and reconciliation starts failing. Monitoring and backups fail with it           | Edit the Secret named in `spec.secretsName`            |
| Edit the `internal-<cluster-name>` Secret                                               | That Secret is the Operator record of what it has already applied. Editing it makes the Operator believe a password is in place that MySQL does not have | Leave it unchanged. Edit the user Secret instead       |
| Run `DROP USER` or rename a system user                                                 | Backups, monitoring, the proxies, and the Operator itself authenticate as these users                                                                    | Leave the system users in place. They are not optional |
| Delete the user Secret to regenerate passwords                                          | The Operator cannot authenticate to apply new passwords                                                                                                  | Edit the password values in place                      |
| Grant application privileges to `root` or `operator` and use them from your application | Password rotation then takes your application down with the cluster                                                                                      | Declare an application user in `spec.users`            |

## Storage

Request a larger volume in the CR. The Operator grows the PVCs when volume expansion is enabled and the StorageClass supports it. See [Resize storage](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/scaling-storage-resize.html).

**What the Operator does:**

- Grows PVCs when you increase the size in the CR, when `storageScaling.enableVolumeScaling` is on and the StorageClass supports expansion.
- Grows storage automatically when `spec.storageScaling.autoscaling` is enabled. When disk usage crosses the trigger threshold (80% by default), storage grows by the configured step, up to the configured maximum.
- Detects a failed resize and reverts the volume template so the CR matches reality again.

**What you still do:**

- Choose a StorageClass with `allowVolumeExpansion: true`. Without it, the size in the CR and the size on disk never agree.
- Watch disk usage, and set a maximum that your quota can satisfy.
- Take over PVC sizes yourself if you set `enableExternalAutoscaling`. The Operator then stops managing PVC sizes and leaves them to your external controller.

**Never do this manually:**

| Do not                                        | What goes wrong                                                                                                                                                                          | Do this instead                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Edit or patch a PVC directly                  | The Operator reconciles PVC sizes against the CR. Your change is reverted, or it conflicts with a resize in progress                                                                     | Change the storage size in the CR                                                           |
| Try to shrink storage                         | The Operator rejects the shrink. It reverts the volume template and reports that the requested size is below the actual size                                                             | Shrinking is not supported. Back up, recreate the cluster with smaller volumes, and restore |
| Delete a PVC to reclaim space or reset a node | The data is gone. The replacement node needs a full state transfer from a healthy donor, which loads that donor. If the cluster was already degraded, this can remove the last good copy | Grow the volume, or remove data from inside the database                                    |

## Cross-site replication

Describe the replication channels in the CR. See [Set up cross-site replication](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/replication.html).

**What the Operator does:**

- Sets up the asynchronous replication channels you list in `spec.pxc.replicationChannels`.
- Stops and removes replication channels that are not in the list.
- Logs `Replication for channel is not running` when a channel stops. It doesn’t repair the channel.

**What you still do:**

- Provide routable endpoints between the sites, and matching replication passwords.
- Monitor replication. If it breaks, you fix it.

**Never do this manually:**

| Do not                                                                  | What goes wrong                                                                                             | Do this instead           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| Create a replication channel in MySQL on a cluster the Operator manages | The Operator stops the channel and removes its sources, because it is not in `spec.pxc.replicationChannels` | Add the channel to the CR |

## Database upgrades

Let the Operator move nodes one at a time. See [About upgrades](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/update.html) and [Upgrade Percona XtraDB Cluster](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/update-db.html).

**What the Operator does:**

- **SmartUpdate.** The Operator upgrades Percona XtraDB Cluster nodes one at a time, keeps quorum, and restarts the primary last to minimize connection disruption.
- Waits for the proxies to be Ready before it begins.
- Checks the Percona Version Service for available versions when `spec.upgradeOptions.apply` enables that check.
- **Refuses to start an upgrade while a backup is running.**

**What you still do:**

- Decide when to upgrade, and test the target version first.
- Review release notes for changes that affect your configuration.
- **Upgrade in order.** Upgrade the Operator first, then raise `spec.crVersion` in the Custom Resource. Upgrading the Operator alone does not change the database images. The Operator also keeps some behavior of an existing cluster tied to its `crVersion`, so new behavior of those features starts only after you raise it. See [Upgrade CRD and the Operator](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/update-operator.html).
- Choose whether automatic version updates are appropriate. `upgradeOptions.apply` is `Disabled` by default. Set it to `Recommended`, `Latest` or an exact version to let the Operator upgrade the database. For production clusters, pin a version and upgrade deliberately. See [Automatic minor upgrades](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/update-automatic.html).
- **Major version upgrades.** Treat a major version upgrade as a planned operation with its own procedure. Follow [Upgrade Percona XtraDB Cluster](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/update-db.html).

**Never do this manually:**

| Do not                                                                            | What goes wrong                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Do this instead                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Change `spec.updateStrategy` to `RollingUpdate` to make an upgrade go faster      | Kubernetes still restarts the Pods in order and waits for each one to be ready. But it doesn’t wait for a running backup or for ProxySQL, doesn’t require a ready proxy, and doesn’t stop when a Pod can’t start. The Operator’s checks are skipped | Leave the strategy on `SmartUpdate` and find out what the upgrade is waiting for                                                                                                                                                       |
| Edit the image tag to jump a major version                                        | Skipping the documented upgrade path can leave the data dictionary in a state the new version cannot read                                                                                                                                           | Follow the database upgrade procedure                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Delete Pods during an upgrade to unstick it                                       | SmartUpdate tracks which node it has reached. Restarting nodes underneath it breaks that sequence                                                                                                                                                   | Check the Operator logs. An upgrade that waits on a running backup, or on a proxy that is not Ready, is working as intended. See [Check the logs](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug-logs.html) |
| Run different Percona XtraDB Cluster versions across nodes for an extended period | Mixed-version clusters are safe only for the duration of an upgrade                                                                                                                                                                                 | Complete the upgrade                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

## Stay inside safe operating limits

The Operator rejects a CR that breaks the Percona XtraDB Cluster size limits or runs without TLS.

| Setting                                    | Safe limit    | Why                                                                                |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `spec.pxc.size`                            | At least 3    | Galera needs three nodes to hold quorum when one is lost                           |
| `spec.pxc.size`                            | At most 5     | Write latency grows with every node that must certify a transaction                |
| `spec.pxc.size`                            | An odd number | An even-sized cluster can split into two halves with no majority                   |
| `spec.haproxy.size` / `spec.proxysql.size` | At least 2    | A single proxy is a single point of failure in front of a highly available cluster |
| `spec.tls.enabled`                         | `true`        | Replication traffic between nodes is otherwise unencrypted                         |

Read more about node count in [Design and architecture](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture.html).

You can turn each check off individually under `spec.unsafeFlags`. See [Override a safety check](#override-a-safety-check). Do not turn a check off to clear an error message.

## Override a safety check

`spec.unsafeFlags` turns off individual safety checks. Each check exists because turning it off can lose data or availability. Field details are in the [Unsafe flags section](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator.html#operator-unsafeflags-section).

| Flag                            | Enables                                                                             | What you give up                                                           |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unsafeFlags.pxcSize`           | Fewer than three, more than five, or an even number of Percona XtraDB Cluster nodes | Quorum guarantees. A cluster with one or two nodes is not highly available |
| `unsafeFlags.proxySize`         | A single HAProxy or ProxySQL Pod                                                    | Proxy redundancy. A proxy restart is an outage                             |
| `unsafeFlags.tls`               | Running without TLS                                                                 | Encryption of replication and client traffic                               |
| `unsafeFlags.backupIfUnhealthy` | Backups from a cluster that is not Ready                                            | Confidence that the backup is consistent and restorable                    |

The older `allowUnsafeConfigurations` option turns on all four flags at once.

Use these flags for a development cluster, a local test, or a deliberate single-node setup for continuous integration. On a production cluster, an Operator rejection describes a real risk in the configuration you asked for.

## Check before you intervene

When a manual change looks necessary, do the following:

1. Check whether the CR already exposes what you want. Most requests for manual changes are covered by a field.
1. Reproduce the change on a non-production cluster first.
1. Capture the Operator logs and the resource status before you change anything. See [Check the logs](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug-logs.html).
1. Contact [Percona Support](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/get-help.html) before you act on a production cluster.

Manual intervention on a running database cluster is recoverable far less often than it looks from the outside.

# How the Operator reacts to changes

This page explains what the Operator does after you change the [Custom Resource](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#custom-resource): when it acts, in which order, which changes restart Pods, and what the cluster status tells you while the change is applied.

## What a reconcile is

The `PerconaXtraDBCluster` Custom Resource describes the *desired state* of the cluster. A *reconcile* is one pass of the Operator over the cluster: it reads the Custom Resource, compares it with the *actual state* of the Kubernetes objects and the database, and changes whatever differs. Reconciles repeat continuously, so the cluster converges to the Custom Resource even if a single pass cannot finish the job.

## What triggers a reconcile

- **A change to the Custom Resource**, or to the users Secret named in `spec.secretsName`.
- **A periodic re-check.** After each successful pass, the Operator reconciles the cluster again about 5 seconds later. Because of this, manual edits to the objects the Operator manages, such as a [StatefulSet](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#statefulset) or a Service, are reverted within seconds. Make changes in the Custom Resource instead.
- **A retry after an error.** If a pass fails, the Operator retries it with an increasing delay.

Why the Operator seems to do nothing after an error

After a failed pass, the Operator doesn’t re-check the cluster every 5 seconds. It retries with an exponential backoff: the delay starts at a few milliseconds and doubles with each consecutive failure, up to about 16 minutes. The delay resets only after a successful pass. So if a reconcile has been failing for a while and you then fix the cause, for example create a missing Secret, the Operator may not notice it for several minutes.

Any change to the Custom Resource starts a new pass immediately. To trigger one without changing the configuration, add or update an annotation:

```
kubectl annotate pxc cluster1 percona.com/reconcile-trigger="$(date +%s)" --overwrite
```

The annotation name is arbitrary; the Operator doesn’t read it. Restarting the Operator Pod also resets the backoff.

Only one Operator Pod is active at a time; if you run several replicas, they elect a leader. The Operator watches the namespaces listed in the `WATCH_NAMESPACE` environment variable, or all namespaces if it is empty. See [Single-namespace and multi-namespace deployment](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/cluster-wide.html).

The `MAX_CONCURRENT_RECONCILES` environment variable of the Operator Deployment sets how many objects of each kind the Operator reconciles in parallel. It applies separately to clusters, backups and restores. The default is `1`: the Operator reconciles one cluster at a time, and other clusters wait in the queue. A pass can take long, because a [Smart Update](#how-smart-update-works) waits inside the pass for each restarted Pod. If you run many clusters with one Operator, raise this value. See [Configure concurrency for a cluster reconciliation](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/reconciliation-concurrency.html) and [`MAX_CONCURRENT_RECONCILES`](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/env-vars-operator.html#max_concurrent_reconciles).

## Order of operations

Each reconcile runs the same steps in the same order. Knowing the order helps you understand why one change waits for another: for example, a storage resize in progress delays the rest of the pass.

```
flowchart TD
  A["Validate the Custom Resource<br/>and apply defaults"] --> B{"Cluster being<br/>deleted?"}
  B -- "yes" --> B1["Run finalizers, stop"]
  B -- "no" --> C["Check for a full cluster crash"]
  C --> D["Users and passwords"]
  D --> E["Storage: autoscaling, PVC resize"]
  E --> F["TLS certificates"]
  F --> G["StatefulSets, ConfigMaps,<br/>PodDisruptionBudgets"]
  G --> H["Smart Update: restart<br/>outdated database Pods"]
  H --> I["Services"]
  I --> J["Cross-site replication channels"]
  J --> K["Backup schedules, binlog collector,<br/>binlog gap check"]
  K --> L["Update status, re-check in 5 s"]
```

## What happens when I change a field

| Field                                                                                         | What the Operator does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Restart?                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pxc.size`, `haproxy.size`, `proxysql.size`                                                   | Changes the number of replicas. The new size must pass the safety checks, see [Unsafe configurations](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/architecture-responsibilities.html#unsafe-configurations)                                                    | No                                                                  |
| Image, resources, environment variables, affinity, sidecars                                   | Updates the Pod template                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Yes, a rolling restart; for database Pods in the Smart Update order |
| `pxc.configuration`                                                                           | Updates the ConfigMap. The `percona.com/configuration-hash` annotation on the Pods changes                                                                                                                                                                                             | Yes                                                                 |
| Contents of the TLS Secrets, the Vault Secret, or the environment variables Secret            | The hash annotations on the Pods change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Yes                                                                 |
| A system user password in the users Secret                                                    | Changes the password in the database, then restarts only the components that use this user. See [System users](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/users.html#system-users)                                                                            | Yes, selectively                                                    |
| Storage size, `pxc.volumeSpec.persistentVolumeClaim.resources.requests.storage` (larger only) | Patches the PVCs and recreates the StatefulSet without deleting its Pods. Requires `storageScaling.enableVolumeScaling`. See [Resize storage](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/scaling-storage-resize.html)                                         | No                                                                  |
| `haproxy.enabled`, `proxysql.enabled`                                                         | Creates or deletes the proxy StatefulSet and Services. HAProxy has no PVCs. The ProxySQL PVCs are kept unless the `percona.com/delete-proxysql-pvc` finalizer is set. See [Switch the proxy](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/proxy-switching.html) | Proxy Pods only                                                     |
| `pause: true`                                                                                 | Scales all components to 0 and removes the binlog collector                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Pods stop                                                           |
| `tls.enabled`                                                                                 | Pauses the cluster, changes the certificates, and starts the cluster again                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Full stop and start                                                 |
| `upgradeOptions.apply`                                                                        | On the `upgradeOptions.schedule`, checks for new versions and writes new images into the Custom Resource, which triggers a Smart Update                                                                                                                                                | Yes, when a new version is applied                                  |

## Update strategies

When a change requires restarting Pods, the `updateStrategy` option in the Custom Resource decides how it happens. See also [Update strategies](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/update.html#update-strategies).

- **`SmartUpdate`** (default). The Operator restarts database Pods itself, one at a time, and is aware of the client traffic: it asks the proxy which node currently receives writes and restarts that node last. With ProxySQL, it also waits until each restarted node is back in its hostgroup before it moves on. Proxy Pods use a regular Kubernetes rolling update.
- **`RollingUpdate`**. Kubernetes restarts the Pods with a native StatefulSet rolling update, without [Galera](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#galera) awareness. It waits for each Pod to become ready, but it doesn’t pause for a running backup, doesn’t wait for ProxySQL to bring the node online, doesn’t require a ready proxy, and doesn’t stop early when a Pod can’t start.
- **`OnDelete`**. Nothing restarts until you delete a Pod; Kubernetes then recreates it with the new configuration. See [Manual upgrade](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/update_manually.html).

### How Smart Update works

```
sequenceDiagram
  participant O as Operator
  participant P2 as cluster1-pxc-2
  participant P1 as cluster1-pxc-1
  participant P0 as cluster1-pxc-0 (writer)
  Note over O: Pods run an outdated revision.<br/>Is a backup running? Then wait.
  O->>P2: delete Pod
  P2-->>O: recreated, Ready and Synced
  O->>P1: delete Pod
  P1-->>O: recreated, Ready and Synced
  O->>P0: delete Pod (writer last)
  P0-->>O: recreated, Ready and Synced
  Note over O: rollout complete
```

1. The Operator waits while a backup is `Starting` or `Running`. A Smart Update never restarts nodes under a running backup.
1. It asks the proxy which node is the writer. With HAProxy, it connects through the `cluster1-haproxy` Service and reads the host name of the node it lands on. With ProxySQL, it reads the writer hostgroup. Usually the writer is `cluster1-pxc-0`, but after a failover it can be another node.
1. It restarts the other nodes first, from the highest number down.
1. After each restart, it waits until the Pod is ready and its node is `Synced` with the cluster. With ProxySQL, it also waits until the node is back in its hostgroup (the writer hostgroup for `cluster1-pxc-0`, the reader hostgroup for the others) and ProxySQL marks it `ONLINE`.
1. It restarts the writer last, so writes fail over only once during the rollout.

Smart Update requires an enabled proxy (HAProxy or ProxySQL) that is ready. It stops waiting and reports a failure if a restarted Pod is in `ImagePullBackOff`, `ErrImagePull` or `CrashLoopBackOff`, or cannot be scheduled for more than 2 minutes. If a node does not become `Synced`, the Operator keeps waiting for up to 2 hours, or for `pxc.livenessProbes.initialDelaySeconds` seconds if you changed that value from the default. While it waits, the Operator logs show what it is waiting for.

### Automatic upgrades

With `upgradeOptions.apply` set to `Recommended`, `Latest` or a specific version, the Operator checks the Percona Version Service on the `upgradeOptions.schedule` (by default, daily at 04:00) and, if a new version is available, writes the new images into the Custom Resource. The Smart Update then rolls them out. The check runs only when the cluster is `ready`. The default value `Disabled` turns automatic upgrades off. See [Automatic minor upgrades](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/update-automatic.html).

Upgrade the Operator itself and its CRDs before you raise `spec.crVersion`. See [Upgrade CRD and the Operator](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/update-operator.html).

## Status

The `status.state` field of the Custom Resource has one of these values:

| State          | Meaning                                                                                                          |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `initializing` | The cluster is starting, a change is being applied, or at least one database or proxy Pod is not ready           |
| `ready`        | The cluster matches the Custom Resource and serves traffic                                                       |
| `paused`       | `spec.pause` is `true` and all Pods are stopped                                                                  |
| `stopping`     | Pods are being stopped, for example while the cluster pauses                                                     |
| `error`        | The last reconcile failed. The reason is in a condition with the reason `ErrorReconcile` and in `status.message` |

### What `ready` means

The cluster is `ready` only when all of the following are true:

- Every database Pod and every Pod of the enabled proxy has all containers ready.
- Every one of these Pods runs the current revision of its StatefulSet, so no rollout is pending.
- The cluster endpoint, `status.host`, is known. For a `LoadBalancer` Service, this means the cloud provider has assigned an address.

### Why a cluster stays in `initializing`

If the cluster stays in `initializing` for a long time, one of the conditions above is not met. A `ready` cluster also goes back to `initializing` as soon as one of its Pods becomes unready, for example after a container restart. Compare `status.pxc.ready` with `status.pxc.size`, and the same fields under `status.haproxy` or `status.proxysql`, to see which component is affected. The usual causes:

- **A rollout is pending.** Some Pods still run the previous revision, for example because a Smart Update is waiting for a backup to finish or for a node to become `Synced`. Check the Operator logs.
- **A database node isn’t `Synced`.** The node is still receiving an [SST](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#sst), or it cannot join the cluster. Check the `pxc` container logs.
- **A [PVC](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#pvc) resize is in progress.** The cluster stays in `initializing` until the resize finishes. Check the PVC events.
- **No endpoint has been assigned.** The `LoadBalancer` Service is waiting for the cloud provider. Check `kubectl get svc`.
- **A Pod cannot be scheduled.** The status message shows the scheduler’s reason.

The status does not show everything. If the state looks wrong but there is no message, read the Operator logs. See [Which layer is it?](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug.html#which-layer-is-it).

## Pause

Setting `spec.pause: true` stops the cluster gracefully:

- All database and proxy Pods are scaled down to 0. PVCs and data are kept.
- The binlog collector is removed.
- Smart Updates are not run.
- The status changes to `paused` when all Pods have stopped.

Set `spec.pause: false` to start the cluster again. The Operator also pauses the cluster itself during a restore and when you turn TLS on or off. See [Pause/resume Percona XtraDB Cluster](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/pause.html).

# Key workflows

This page describes the main workflows of the Operator step by step: how client traffic reaches the database and fails over, how backups, point-in-time recovery and restores work, and how the cluster recovers from a full crash. Each section ends with the objects and fields to check when the workflow fails.

The examples use a cluster named `cluster1`.

## Client traffic and proxy failover

### HAProxy

```
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant H as HAProxy
  participant P0 as cluster1-pxc-0
  participant P2 as cluster1-pxc-2
  C->>H: connect to cluster1-haproxy:3306
  H->>P0: writer
  Note over P0: fails the health check twice
  H->>P2: backup server with the highest number
  Note over P0: recovers and is Synced
  H->>H: closes connections to backup servers
  H->>P0: new connections go to pxc-0 again
```

**What happens:**

- The writer is always `cluster1-pxc-0`. HAProxy chooses it by its number, not by its [Galera](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#galera) state. The other nodes are backup servers, listed from the highest number down.
- HAProxy checks every node every 10 seconds. A node passes the check when it belongs to the [primary component](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#primary-component), is `Synced` (or a [donor](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#donor), when it is the only node the proxy knows about or you set `OK_IF_DONOR` to `1`), has `pxc_maint_mode` set to `DISABLED`, and accepts queries. After two failed checks in a row, the node is marked down and HAProxy closes its sessions, so a failure is noticed 10 to 20 seconds after the node stops passing the check (about 15 to 25 seconds after a network failure). HAProxy doesn’t mark a node down because a connection failed.
- When `cluster1-pxc-0` is down, writes go to the node with the highest number, for example `cluster1-pxc-2`.
- When `cluster1-pxc-0` passes the check again, HAProxy closes the connections to the backup server and new connections go to `cluster1-pxc-0`. Applications must reconnect. If `cluster1-pxc-0` was restarted, the failback happens when `pxc-monit` adds it back to the configuration (see [Node discovery](#node-discovery)).
- The `cluster1-haproxy-replicas` Service (port 3306 on the Service, 3307 in HAProxy) spreads connections across all nodes in round-robin. To exclude `cluster1-pxc-0` from reads, set [`haproxy.exposeReplicas.onlyReaders`](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator.html#haproxyexposereplicasonlyreaders).
- Port 3309 accepts connections that use the [proxy protocol](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/haproxy-conf.html#enabling-the-proxy-protocol).

### ProxySQL

In native mode, ProxySQL works in single-writer mode with four hostgroups: 11 for the writer, 10 for readers, 12 for backup writers, and 13 for offline nodes. The writer is `cluster1-pxc-0`, with the highest write weight (1000000, against 1000 minus the Pod number for the others) and the lowest read weight. The ProxySQL Pods form a ProxySQL cluster and share their configuration. With the external scheduler enabled, weighted writer selection prefers `cluster1-pxc-0`, and ProxySQL clustering is disabled. See [Configuring load balancing with ProxySQL](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/proxysql-conf.html) and [ProxySQL scheduler](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/proxysql-conf.html#proxysql-scheduler-tech-preview).

### Node discovery

Both proxies learn about the database nodes the same way. The `pxc-monit` container in each proxy Pod looks up the headless `cluster1-pxc` Service in DNS every second. The Service lists only ready database Pods. The first update is applied immediately. After that, updates are applied at most once every 30 seconds, so a node that leaves or joins the cluster is reflected in the proxy configuration within about 2 to 35 seconds. After each reload, HAProxy closes the sessions still open on the previous configuration after 10 seconds (`hard-stop-after 10s`), including sessions to healthy nodes.

**Where to look if it fails:**

- `kubectl get endpoints cluster1-pxc` shows which database Pods the proxies can see.
- `kubectl logs cluster1-haproxy-0 -c pxc-monit` (or `cluster1-proxysql-0`) shows the node list and configuration reloads.
- `kubectl logs cluster1-haproxy-0 -c haproxy` shows health check results.
- See also [In-cluster failover](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/failover-in-cluster.html) and [Configure load balancing](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/load-balancing.html).
- More symptoms and the layer that owns each: [Initial troubleshooting](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug.html#where-to-look-first).

## On-demand backup

```
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant O as Operator
  participant L as Lease backup-lock<br/>(only if allowParallel is false)
  participant J as Job xb-backup1
  participant D as Donor node
  participant S as Storage
  U->>O: create PerconaXtraDBClusterBackup "backup1"
  O->>O: check storage and cluster state
  O->>L: take the lock
  O->>J: create the Job
  J->>D: join as Galera arbitrator, request SST
  D->>J: stream the data
  J->>S: upload the backup
  J-->>O: Job completed
  O->>L: release the lock
  O->>U: status Succeeded
```

**What happens:**

1. You create a `PerconaXtraDBClusterBackup` object. See [Make on-demand backup](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-ondemand.html).
1. The Operator checks the storage configuration and waits until the cluster is `ready`. To back up a cluster that isn’t `ready`, set `unsafeFlags.backupIfUnhealthy`.
1. Backups run in parallel by default. If you set [`backup.allowParallel`](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/operator.html#backupallowparallel) to `false`, the Operator takes the `pxc-cluster1-backup-lock` [Lease](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#lease), so that backups don’t overlap. Other backups wait with an empty `status.state` until the lock is free. See [Multiple backups](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups.html#multiple-backups).
1. The Operator creates the Job `xb-backup1` and sets the state to `Starting`. The Job runs the Galera [arbitrator](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#arbitrator) (`garbd`), joins the cluster, and requests a full [SST](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#sst). The donor is a `Synced` node other than the writer `cluster1-pxc-0`, usually the node with the highest number. While it sends the data, the donor node is in the `Donor` state.
1. The Job streams the data to S3-compatible storage or Azure, or to a new [PVC](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#pvc).
1. The Operator releases the lock, if it took one, and sets the backup status.

The backup goes through these states:

- Empty: the backup object exists, but the Job isn’t created yet. The Operator waits for the cluster to be `ready` or, with `allowParallel: false`, for the lock.
- `Starting`: the Job is created and waits to start copying data.
- `Suspended`: the cluster became unhealthy, so the Operator suspended the Job. It resumes when the cluster is `ready` again. See [Backup suspension](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups.html#backup-suspension-for-an-unhealthy-database-cluster).
- `Running`: the Job is copying data.
- `Succeeded` or `Failed`.

`startingDeadlineSeconds` limits the time from backup object creation until the Job is created, that is, while the state is empty. It has no default, so without it a backup waits without a time limit. `runningDeadlineSeconds` limits the time from Job creation until the backup reaches `Running`. Its default is 1200 seconds. `suspendedDeadlineSeconds` limits time spent suspended. The Job’s `activeDeadlineSeconds` limits its active duration. When a configured deadline is exceeded, the backup is marked `Failed`. See [Backup Custom Resource options](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backup-cr.html).

When you delete a backup object, the `percona.com/delete-backup` [finalizer](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#finalizer) removes the backup files from storage first.

XtraBackup sidecar method (tech preview)

With the `XtrabackupSidecar` feature gate turned on, each database Pod runs an `xtrabackup` sidecar container. The backup Job asks the sidecar on a non-primary ready Pod to make the backup, and the node doesn’t enter the `Donor` state. See [XtraBackup sidecar method](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-methods.html#xtrabackup-sidecar-method-tech-preview).

**Where to look if it fails:**

- `kubectl get pxc-backup backup1 -o yaml`: the state, and the conditions.
- `kubectl logs job/xb-backup1`: errors from the backup itself, such as wrong storage credentials or an unreachable endpoint.
- `kubectl get lease pxc-cluster1-backup-lock -o yaml`: which backup holds the lock.
- Operator logs: `Cluster is not ready for backup` means the backup waits for the cluster.
- More symptoms and the layer that owns each: [Initial troubleshooting](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug.html#where-to-look-first).

## Scheduled backups

Scheduled backups are not Kubernetes CronJobs. The Operator keeps the schedules from `backup.schedule` in its own memory and, when a run is due, creates a regular backup object named `cron-cluster1-<storage>-<timestamp>-<hash>`, where the hash is calculated from the schedule expression. From there, the backup follows the [on-demand workflow](#on-demand-backup).

- **If the cluster isn’t `ready` when a run is due, the run is skipped.** No backup object and no event is created. Only the Operator log shows it, with the message `Cluster is not ready for backup. Scheduled backup is not created`.
- **The schedule runs only while the Operator runs.** No backups are created while the Operator is stopped.
- **Retention.** With `retention` set, the Operator deletes the oldest `Succeeded` backups beyond the configured count. See [Making scheduled backups](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-scheduled.html).

**Where to look if it fails:**

- `kubectl get pxc-backup`: the `cron-*` backups and their states.
- Operator logs: skipped runs and errors creating backups.
- More symptoms and the layer that owns each: [Initial troubleshooting](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug.html#where-to-look-first).

## Point-in-time recovery

```
flowchart LR
  P["Synced database node"] -- "binlogs over port 33062" --> C["cluster1-pitr<br/>binlog collector"]
  C -- "upload every timeBetweenUploads" --> S[("Backup storage")]
  O["Operator"] -- "checks for gaps" --> S
  O -- "PITRReady, latestRestorableTime" --> B["Latest backup object"]
```

**What happens:**

- When you turn on `backup.pitr.enabled` and the cluster is `ready`, the Operator creates the `cluster1-pitr` Deployment.
- At the start of each cycle, the collector picks a `Synced` node, preferring the one with the oldest binlogs, reads its binary logs over the admin port, and uploads them to storage every `backup.pitr.timeBetweenUploads` seconds.
- The Operator checks the uploaded binlogs for gaps. A gap means some transactions are missing, for example because the servers purged binlogs before the collector uploaded them. Then the Operator sets the `PITRReady` condition of the latest backup to `False` with the reason `BinlogGapDetected`. You cannot restore to a point after the gap; take a new full backup.
- The `status.latestRestorableTime` field of the backup shows the latest point you can restore to.
- Point-in-time recovery doesn’t work with backups stored on PVCs.

See [Store binary logs for point-in-time recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-pitr.html).

**Where to look if it fails:**

- `kubectl get pxc-backup <backup> -o yaml`: the `PITRReady` condition and `latestRestorableTime`.
- `kubectl logs deployment/cluster1-pitr`: collector errors, such as storage access problems.
- See [Binlog gaps](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-pitr-restore.html#binlog-gaps).
- More symptoms and the layer that owns each: [Initial troubleshooting](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug.html#where-to-look-first).

## Restore

A restore replaces the data of the whole cluster. You start it by creating a `PerconaXtraDBClusterRestore` object. See [Restore the cluster from a previously saved backup](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-restore.html).

```
stateDiagram-v2
  state "Starting" as Starting
  state "Stopping Cluster" as Stopping
  state "Restoring" as Restoring
  state "Preparing Cluster" as Preparing
  state "Point-in-time recovering" as PITR
  state "Starting Cluster" as StartingCluster
  [*] --> Starting
  Starting --> Stopping: checks passed
  Stopping --> Restoring: cluster paused, PVCs deleted
  Restoring --> Preparing
  Preparing --> PITR: point-in-time target set
  Preparing --> StartingCluster
  PITR --> StartingCluster
  StartingCluster --> Succeeded: cluster ready
  Succeeded --> [*]
  Starting --> Failed
  Stopping --> Failed
  Restoring --> Failed
  Preparing --> Failed
  PITR --> Failed
  StartingCluster --> Failed
  Failed --> [*]
```

**What happens:**

1. **Starting.** The Operator checks the backup, the Secrets, the storage, and the point-in-time target if you set one. Only one restore can run on a cluster at a time. The Operator repeats the basic checks on every pass, so a restore can fail in any state, for example when the cluster or the backup object is deleted while the restore runs.
1. **Stopping Cluster.** The Operator sets `spec.pause: true` on the cluster and waits until all Pods are gone. Then it deletes the PVCs of all database Pods except `datadir-cluster1-pxc-0`.
1. **Restoring.** The Job `restore-job-<restore>-cluster1` writes the backup into the data volume of `cluster1-pxc-0`.
1. **Preparing Cluster.** The Job `prepare-job-*` starts `mysqld` on the restored data, resets the system user passwords to the ones in the cluster’s internal Secret, and removes the Galera state files so that the node starts a new cluster.
1. **Point-in-time recovering** (only with a `pitr` section in the restore). The Operator starts the cluster with one database node and no proxies, so clients cannot connect. The Job `pitr-job-*` replays binlogs up to the target.
1. **Starting Cluster.** The Operator restores the original sizes and unpauses the cluster. The other nodes start with empty volumes and get the data from `cluster1-pxc-0` through SST.
1. **Succeeded** when the cluster has the original sizes, the Operator has applied the latest [Custom Resource](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/glossary.html#custom-resource) generation, and the cluster is `ready`. Until then, the restore waits in **Starting Cluster**, with no time limit. **Failed** when a check fails.

Restore considerations

**A restore deletes data volumes and stops the cluster** The cluster is unavailable for the whole restore. The Operator deletes the PVCs of all database Pods except `cluster1-pxc-0`, overwrites the data on that Pod, and any writes after the backup that point-in-time recovery does not cover are lost.

**A restore doesn’t reset the recovery record.** The restored cluster gets a new Galera cluster UUID, but the Operator keeps the previous `status.recovery` record. [Remove the recovery record after every restore](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/backups-restore-in-place.html#remove-the-recovery-record-after-the-restore), or the Operator refuses the next full cluster crash recovery.

**Where to look if it fails:**

- `kubectl get pxc-restore <restore> -o yaml`: the `state` and the error in `status.comments`.
- `kubectl logs job/restore-job-<restore>-cluster1`, then the logs of the `prepare-job-*` and `pitr-job-*` Jobs, depending on the state where the restore stopped.
- Operator logs.
- More symptoms and the layer that owns each: [Initial troubleshooting](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug.html#where-to-look-first).

## Full cluster crash recovery

A full cluster crash means all database nodes stopped at the same time, for example after a power loss, so no node has a running primary component to join. See [Crash recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/recovery.html).

```
sequenceDiagram
  participant O as Operator
  participant P0 as cluster1-pxc-0
  participant P1 as cluster1-pxc-1
  participant P2 as cluster1-pxc-2
  Note over P0,P2: all nodes stopped, no primary component
  P0->>P0: log FULL_PXC_CLUSTER_CRASH and seqno, wait
  P1->>P1: log FULL_PXC_CLUSTER_CRASH and seqno, wait
  P2->>P2: log FULL_PXC_CLUSTER_CRASH and seqno, wait
  O->>O: wait until all Pods are Running, read seqnos
  Note over O: event FullClusterCrashDetected
  O->>P2: bootstrap the node with the highest seqno
  Note over O: event RecoveryStarted
  P0->>P2: join, get the data by IST or SST
  P1->>P2: join, get the data by IST or SST
```

**What happens:**

1. Each database Pod finds that no other node runs a primary component. It logs `FULL_PXC_CLUSTER_CRASH` and its last committed position (the `seqno`), and waits.
1. With `pxc.autoRecovery: true` (the default), the Operator waits until all database Pods are `Running`, reads their `seqno` values, and picks the node with the highest one. That node has the most recent data.
1. The Operator signals that node to bootstrap a new cluster. The other nodes join it and receive the missing data.

After it signals the node, the Operator records the recovery in the `status.recovery` field of the Custom Resource:

- `clusterUUID`: the Galera cluster UUID of the node it bootstrapped from.
- `lastRecoveryPod`: the Pod it bootstrapped from.
- `lastRecoverySeqNo`: the `seqno` of that Pod.
- `lastRecoveryTime`: when the recovery started.

On the next full crash, the Operator compares the new values with this record. It refuses automatic recovery, and emits the `AutomaticRecoveryRefused` event, if the recovery would risk data loss: if the cluster UUID differs from `clusterUUID`, or the highest `seqno` is lower than `lastRecoverySeqNo`. The event message shows both the recorded and the current values. The Operator doesn’t change the cluster UUID when it recovers the cluster. A [restore](#restore) does: it starts a new Galera cluster with a new UUID and doesn’t reset the record. If the Operator recovered the cluster automatically before the restore, the first full crash after the restore is refused until you remove the record. The same happens after manual changes to the Galera state. See [When the Operator refuses automatic recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/recovery.html#when-the-operator-refuses-automatic-recovery) to clean up the record.

**When you recover manually.** If `pxc.autoRecovery` is `false`, or the Operator refused automatic recovery, the nodes keep waiting. You find the node with the highest `seqno` in the `pxc` container logs and tell it to bootstrap. If the data needs repair first, you can make a node wait instead of restarting by creating a `sleep-forever` file in its data directory. The steps are in [Crash recovery](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/recovery.html) and [Avoid the restart-on-fail loop](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug-shell.html#avoid-the-restart-on-fail-loop-for-percona-xtradb-cluster-containers).

**Where to look if it fails:**

- `kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp`: the `FullClusterCrashDetected`, `RecoveryStarted` and `AutomaticRecoveryRefused` events.
- `kubectl get pxc cluster1 -o jsonpath='{.status.recovery}'`: the previous recovery the Operator compares against.
- `kubectl logs cluster1-pxc-N -c pxc`: the `FULL_PXC_CLUSTER_CRASH` messages and the `seqno` of each node.
- Operator logs.
- More symptoms and the layer that owns each: [Initial troubleshooting](https://docs.percona.com/percona-operator-for-xtradb-cluster/1.20.0/debug.html#where-to-look-first).
